# ScopeView

> Small Canvas charts, trace timelines, and flame graphs with exact source readings and no runtime dependencies (`@scopedb/scopeview`).

ScopeView turns structured `v1` telemetry documents (`line`, `area`, `bar`, `horizontal-bar`, `scatter`, `pie`, `top-list`, `treemap`, `big-number`, `trace`, `profile`) into standalone offline HTML reports or lightweight browser Canvas views without rounding 64-bit integers, collapsing sub-millisecond nanoseconds, or coercing `null` gaps to `0`.

## Agent & CLI Workflow

Requires Node.js 24+. Install globally (`npm install -g @scopedb/scopeview`) or invoke via `npx @scopedb/scopeview`:

1. Inspect the versioned JSON Schema: `scopeview schema > schema.json`
2. Print a canonical example document: `scopeview example trace > trace.json` (valid names: `line`, `area`, `bar`, `horizontal-bar`, `scatter`, `pie`, `top-list`, `treemap`, `big-number`, `trace`, `profile`)
3. Validate generated JSON before rendering: `scopeview validate report.json --json`
4. Render a standalone zero-dependency HTML report: `scopeview render report.json -o report.html --json`

## Data & Precision Invariants

- All document inputs follow the `version: 1` envelope (`kind` for `trace` and `profile`, optional `title` and `description`, plus `data` + `spec`, `spans`, or `frames`).
- Numeric values and timestamps can be encoded as strings so `int64`, `uint64`, high-precision decimals, and nanosecond epochs (`> 2^53 - 1`) survive JSON parsing without IEEE-754 rounding.
- Metric series preserve explicit `null` slots as data gaps instead of coercing missing observations to `0`.
- Trace spans preserve `startTimeNs` and `endTimeNs` exact nanosecond strings (including `1 ns` and `0 ns` spans), and CPU profiles preserve `BigInt` frame weights (`selfWeight`) alongside `file` and `line` metadata.
